meta.title: Codex × Clink — Pre-Approved Payments for Async Agent Tasks
meta.description: Codex runs tasks while you're away. Clink adds a scoped payment path approved up front, so the first paid API doesn't stall the run.
meta.ogDescription: Codex works in the background. Clink makes sure the budget and scope are approved before the run starts—not after something stalls.

hero.h1: Codex Can Buy What the Run Needs—While You're Away.
hero.standfirst: Background tasks don't pause to ask. Clink lets you approve the payment scope before the run starts, so Codex can pass a paid dependency and keep the receipts in the task log.

capabilities.title: Asynchronous Tasks Need Pre-Approved Payments.
capabilities.body: An agent that works while you're away cannot stop at every checkout. Clink moves the approval to task start: you define the scope, Codex operates inside it, and the run shows every line.

blocks.title: The Brief Carries the Budget.
blocks.body: State the outcome and the spend ceiling together. Codex carries both into the run, so a paid dependency is a decision the task can make against rules you already set.

visual.heading: Task brief
visual.prompt: Evaluate these three log-parsing APIs against our sample set. If one requires a paid plan to test, buy the cheapest monthly tier under $30.

blocks.title: Approved Up Front, Enforced at Payment.
blocks.body: The scope you set at task start is what the payment honors—merchant type, amount, and purpose. Nothing outside that envelope is spendable, even when nobody is watching.

blocks.title: The Task Log Shows the Money.
blocks.body: When you review the run, the payments sit next to the commits: what was bought, under which instruction, and what it unblocked.

setup.title: Teach Your Agent to Buy.
setup.body: Connect the agent you already use to Clink through MCP. Connector setup is coming next.
setup.thenAsk: “Evaluate the three APIs in the brief. If a paid tier is required to test, buy the cheapest monthly under $30.”

useCases.title: Overnight Runs Shouldn't Stop at a Checkout.

items.title: Keep Long Tasks Fed With Credits
items.body: A run that needs more model capacity buys it inside the ceiling instead of ending incomplete.

items.title: Buy a Paid Tool Mid-Run
items.body: When the evaluation calls for a gated tool, Codex purchases access per use and keeps the output verifiable.

items.title: Stay Inside the Task Budget
items.body: The ceiling from the brief is enforced at payment time—no judgment calls, no surprises in the log.

items.title: Pay per Use, Skip New Subscriptions
items.body: Per-purchase authorization means testing a service doesn't start a recurring relationship you have to unwind.

items.title: Night Runs Self-Serve
items.body: Work scheduled outside office hours proceeds within the approved envelope and files everything for morning review.

items.title: Receipts Where the Code Lives
items.body: Payments appear in the run timeline next to the commits they unblocked—review is one pass, not two systems.

howTo.title: Approve the Scope. Review the Run.
howTo.description: The approval moves to the start of the task, which is what makes an unattended run safe.

steps.name: Write the Brief With the Budget
steps.text: Outcome, ceiling, and any merchant constraints go into the task brief itself—before the run begins.

steps.name: Approve the Purchase Scope Up Front
steps.text: This is the asynchronous difference: the scope is locked before Codex starts, so mid-run purchases never need a human in the loop.

steps.name: Review the Run and the Receipts
steps.text: Payments appear in the task timeline next to the work they unblocked, each traceable to the instruction that authorized it.

faqs.q: What Happens When Codex Needs to Pay While I'm Away?
faqs.a: It can only pay inside the scope you approved at task start—merchant type, amount, and purpose. Anything outside that envelope pauses the task for your review instead of spending.

faqs.q: Does Codex See My Card Details?
faqs.a: No. Clink tokenizes the credential at connection and releases a per-purchase credential against the approved instruction. Codex never handles raw card data.

faqs.q: Can I Cap the Total Spend per Task?
faqs.a: Yes. The ceiling lives in the task brief and is enforced at payment time, so a run can be bounded regardless of how many purchases it attempts.

finalCta.title: Put Codex on Tasks That Need to Spend.
finalCta.description: Approve the payment scope up front and let unattended runs pass paid dependencies without stopping.
